expansion:
A. Thyroid eye disease is correct. This is the characteristic chronic bilateral orbitopathy: progressive bilateral proptosis, gritty foreign-body sensation and tearing/lacrimation, conjunctival congestion, upper-lid retraction producing a staring appearance, and restrictive extraocular-muscle disease. The lecture lists “Grittiness, red eyes, lacrimation” in thyroid eye disease (L10, slide 16), illustrates bilateral lid retraction as Dalrymple and Kocher signs (L10, slide 17), and shows “bilateral proptosis with lid retraction” (L10, slide 18). It also identifies restrictive myopathy with bilateral lid retraction and proptosis in thyroid eye disease (L10, slide 19), which accounts for limited upward gaze.

B. Orbital cellulitis can cause proptosis, conjunctival injection and painful ophthalmoplegia, but it is an acute infection rather than a progressive bilateral presentation. The lecture describes marked pyrexia, tender warm erythematous lids, painful ophthalmoplegia, and infection usually arising from the ethmoid sinuses (L10, slide 26). These infectious features and the classic thyroid lid signs are not present here.

C. Cavernous sinus thrombosis may produce bilateral proptosis, chemosis, venous congestion and ocular-motility signs, but its onset is rapid and it is associated with severe headache, malaise, nausea and vomiting after infection such as sinusitis, cellulitis or otitis (L10, slide 32). That acute, systemically unwell pattern does not fit this progressive thyroid eye disease vignette.

D. Myasthenia gravis causes variable, fatigable ptosis and extraocular-muscle weakness, not lid retraction with proptosis. The course material demonstrates fatigability by lid drooping after sustained upgaze (L5, slide 13) and states that myasthenia may imitate nerve or muscle palsy (L30, slide 20). It does not explain the bilateral protrusion, congestion, and thyroid-pattern lid retraction here.
objective: Recognize thyroid eye disease from bilateral progressive proptosis, lid retraction, ocular-surface symptoms, and restrictive ocular motility.
